newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Somar sees reduced weather risk for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Somar sees reduced weather risk for coffee.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions now look much less likely to see damaging cold over the weekend, with a larger polar air mass breaking into two smaller masses, local metereologist Somar said Tuesday.

Somar said Monday an air mass of around 1,032 millibars could pass through the country's coffee regions from the evening of July 5, provoking a sharp drop in temperatures, possibly to zero degrees Celsius in some regions.

However according to the latest models, a first air mass of only 1,028 millibars would cause temperatures to fall to six degrees Celsius in north Parana during the night of July 5/early morning July 6, Somar forecaster Marcos Massari said Tuesday.
Minimum temperatures in the south of Minas Gerais in the early morning of July 7 should be between five and eight degrees Celsius, he added.
"With these temperatures, there is no great danger of frosts for coffee," Massari said.

The air mass should start to head out to the ocean on July 6 and then the main air mass, now expected to have an intensity of 1,026 millibars, should pass quickly through the far south of Brazil on July 7, without any detrimental impact on coffee.
U.S. forecasters have this week been forecasting cooler temperatures but no damaging cold in sight for Brazilian coffee areas.
